crops.name: Oilseed rape (winter)
crops.overview: The main Irish oilseed and a valuable break crop before wheat.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.N: 160–220 kg N/ha total incl. 30 kg autumn (Teagasc OSR guide); 30–40 kg S/ha
conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: High N demand is hard to meet organically: grow after clover-rich ley or legumes and apply slurry/FYM in spring. Sulphur from permitted elemental S or gypsum.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.critical: Flowering and pod fill (Apr–June for winter OSR).

harvest.signs: Seeds dark brown/black in 2/3 of pods; desiccate or swath

conventional.pests: Cabbage stem flea beetle, pollen beetle, slugs, light leaf spot, phoma, sclerotinia. Spray only above thresholds.

organic.pests: Sow early into good seedbeds for vigour, companion crops (e.g. buckwheat/berseem) to confuse flea beetle, wide rotation (1 in 5) against clubroot and sclerotinia.
organic.weeds: Wide rows with inter-row hoeing; competitive early canopy.

crops.rotation: 1 year in 4–5 (clubroot). Excellent break crop before wheat.

crops.name: Field beans (winter)
crops.overview: Protein crop; DAFM Protein Aid scheme supports it.

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: No N needed (fixes its own). P/K from FYM or permitted rock phosphate/potassium sulphate if index 1.
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–7.5; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Rain-fed; beans tolerate heavier land, peas need free drainage.

conventional.pests: Bean weevil, black bean aphid, chocolate spot, downy mildew (beans); pea moth, pea aphid (peas).

organic.pests: Resistant/tolerant varieties, later sowing of spring beans to avoid weevil peak, encourage ladybirds and hoverflies (field margins).
organic.weeds: Blind harrowing before emergence, inter-row hoeing; good seedbed.

crops.rotation: 1 in 5 years (foot rots, sclerotinia). Leaves N for the next cereal.

crops.name: Quinoa

soil.index: Aim for P and K index 3 (Teagasc). Take a soil test every 4–5 years.

conventional.S: Sulphur 15–25 kg/ha on light soils/high-yield crops
conventional.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–8.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.
conventional.manures: Account for slurry/FYM nutrients (Teagasc Green Book values) and stay within Nitrates Regulations limits (170 kg/ha organic N whole-farm; derogation rules apply).
conventional.timing: Apply P & K at or before sowing; split N to match crop demand. Observe closed periods for fertiliser and slurry.

organic.text: Moderate: compost; avoid excess N (nitrates in leaf).
organic.lime: Lime to keep pH 6.0–8.0; apply ground limestone per soil test (typically 2.5–7.5 t/ha), ideally a few months before sowing.

water.rainfall: Shallow roots: frequent light watering in dry spells; bolting if dry.

harvest.storage: Short — cool quickly and keep at 0–2°C.

conventional.pests: Aphids, slugs, downy mildew, tipburn, bolting.

organic.pests: Successional sowing, mesh, slug traps/ferric phosphate pellets (permitted), mildew-resistant varieties.

crops.rotation: Fits anywhere; avoid same family repeat.
